findings.title: Broken internal link
findings.evidence: https://shop.example.com/error returned HTTP 500. Linked from 1 page(s), anchor text "Status": https://shop.example.com/
findings.explanation: One or more pages link to an internal URL that returned an error status.
findings.suggestion: Update or remove the broken links on the linking pages, or redirect the broken URL to a relevant live page.

findings.title: Missing title tag
findings.evidence: No <title> element found in the HTML <head>.
findings.explanation: The page has no <title> element. Titles are a primary source for the clickable headline in search results.
findings.suggestion: Add a unique, descriptive <title> (roughly 30–60 characters) that includes the page's main topic.

findings.title: Broken internal link
findings.evidence: https://shop.example.com/missing returned HTTP 404. Linked from 2 page(s), anchor text "Gift cards": https://shop.example.com/, https://shop.example.com/blog
findings.explanation: One or more pages link to an internal URL that returned an error status.
findings.suggestion: Update or remove the broken links on the linking pages, or redirect the broken URL to a relevant live page.

findings.title: Redirect loop or excessive redirects
findings.evidence: Redirect loop detected. Hops: https://shop.example.com/loop-a → https://shop.example.com/loop-b
findings.explanation: The URL redirects in a loop or exceeds the redirect limit, so it never resolves to a page.
findings.suggestion: Fix the redirect rules so the URL resolves to a single final page in one hop.

findings.title: Redirect chain
findings.evidence: 2 redirects: https://shop.example.com/old-page (301) → https://shop.example.com/redirect-mid (301) → https://shop.example.com/about (200)
findings.explanation: The URL passes through two or more redirects before reaching the final page. Chains slow users down and waste crawl budget.
findings.suggestion: Point the first URL (and any internal links to it) directly at the final destination with a single 301 redirect.

findings.title: Insecure (HTTP) resources on HTTPS page
findings.evidence: 1 insecure resource(s), e.g. http://cdn.example.net/bowl.jpg
findings.explanation: This HTTPS page loads images, scripts, stylesheets or frames over plain HTTP. Browsers may block them or show warnings.
findings.suggestion: Load these resources over HTTPS (or use protocol-relative/relative URLs).

findings.title: Missing viewport meta tag
findings.evidence: No <meta name="viewport"> tag found.
findings.explanation: No <meta name="viewport"> was found, so mobile browsers may render the page at desktop width.
findings.suggestion: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">.

findings.title: Images missing alt attribute
findings.evidence: 1 of 2 images have no alt attribute. Examples: https://shop.example.com/img/team.jpg
findings.explanation: Some elements have no alt attribute at all. Alt text is needed for screen readers and helps image search. (Empty alt="" is correct for decorative images and is not flagged.)
findings.suggestion: Add descriptive alt text to meaningful images, and alt="" to purely decorative ones.

findings.title: Page is set to noindex
findings.evidence: X-Robots-Tag: noindex
findings.explanation: A robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header tells search engines not to index this page. If unintentional, the page cannot appear in search results.
findings.suggestion: If the page should rank, remove 'noindex' from the robots meta tag / X-Robots-Tag header. If intentional, no action is needed.

findings.title: Missing H1 heading
findings.evidence: No <h1> element found in the HTML.
findings.explanation: No <h1> was found in the HTML. A clear main heading helps users and search engines understand the page topic. (Content rendered only by JavaScript is not visible to this crawler.)
findings.suggestion: Add one visible <h1> that states the page's main topic.

findings.title: Missing meta description
findings.evidence: No <meta name="description"> tag found.
findings.explanation: No meta description was found. Search engines may generate a snippet from page text instead; a written description gives you more control over the snippet.
findings.suggestion: Add a unique meta description (roughly 50–160 characters) summarising the page and its value.

findings.title: Duplicate meta description across pages
findings.evidence: "Handmade ceramics and homeware, designed in small batches and shipped worldwide from our studio." is shared by 2 pages: https://shop.example.com/, https://shop.example.com/contact
findings.explanation: Several crawled pages share exactly the same meta description.
findings.suggestion: Write a distinct description for each page.

findings.title: Duplicate meta description across pages
findings.evidence: "Browse our full range." is shared by 2 pages: https://shop.example.com/products, https://shop.example.com/blog
findings.explanation: Several crawled pages share exactly the same meta description.
findings.suggestion: Write a distinct description for each page.

findings.title: Duplicate meta description across pages
findings.evidence: "Handmade ceramics and homeware, designed in small batches and shipped worldwide from our studio." is shared by 2 pages: https://shop.example.com/, https://shop.example.com/contact
findings.explanation: Several crawled pages share exactly the same meta description.
findings.suggestion: Write a distinct description for each page.

findings.title: Duplicate meta description across pages
findings.evidence: "Browse our full range." is shared by 2 pages: https://shop.example.com/products, https://shop.example.com/blog
findings.explanation: Several crawled pages share exactly the same meta description.
findings.suggestion: Write a distinct description for each page.

findings.title: Missing canonical tag
findings.evidence: No <link rel="canonical"> found.
findings.explanation: No rel="canonical" link was found. Canonicals help consolidate duplicate URLs (e.g. with tracking parameters).
findings.suggestion: Add a self-referencing <link rel="canonical"> with the preferred absolute URL.

findings.title: Internal links point to redirecting URLs
findings.evidence: https://shop.example.com/old-page redirects (301) to https://shop.example.com/about. Linked from 1 page(s): https://shop.example.com/
findings.explanation: Internal links point to a URL that redirects. It works, but costs an extra request for every visit and crawl.
findings.suggestion: Update the internal links to point directly at the final URL.

findings.title: Missing html lang attribute
findings.evidence: <html> element has no lang attribute.
findings.explanation: The <html> element has no lang attribute, which helps screen readers and language detection.
findings.suggestion: Add the page language, e.g. <html lang="en">.

findings.title: Skipped heading level
findings.evidence: H2 "Bowls" is followed by H4 "Large bowls".
findings.explanation: The heading hierarchy skips a level (for example an H2 followed directly by an H4). This mainly affects accessibility and document structure.
findings.suggestion: Use heading levels in order (H1 → H2 → H3) to reflect the content outline.

findings.title: Title may be truncated in results
findings.evidence: Title (98 chars): "The Example Shop Journal: Stories, Studio Notes, Glazing Experiments and Behind-the-Scenes Updates"
findings.explanation: The title is longer than 60 characters. Search engines truncate by pixel width, so this is an approximation, not a hard limit.
findings.suggestion: Move the most important words to the front and aim for roughly 30–60 characters.

findings.title: Multiple H1 headings
findings.evidence: 2 H1 headings: "Journal"; "Latest posts"
findings.explanation: The page has more than one <h1>. This is valid HTML and not a confirmed problem, but a single main heading usually gives a clearer structure.
findings.suggestion: Consider keeping one H1 for the main topic and using H2/H3 for sections.

findings.title: Meta description length outside typical range
findings.evidence: Meta description (22 chars): "Browse our full range."
findings.explanation: The description is outside the commonly displayed range of about 50–160 characters. This is guidance only; snippet length varies.
findings.suggestion: Aim for roughly 50–160 characters with the key message first.

findings.title: Meta description length outside typical range
findings.evidence: Meta description (22 chars): "Browse our full range."
findings.explanation: The description is outside the commonly displayed range of about 50–160 characters. This is guidance only; snippet length varies.
findings.suggestion: Aim for roughly 50–160 characters with the key message first.

findings.title: Very short title
findings.evidence: Title (4 chars): "Shop"
findings.explanation: The title is shorter than 15 characters, which may not describe the page well.
findings.suggestion: Expand the title to describe the page's topic (and brand, if useful).

findings.title: Low word count
findings.evidence: 5 words of visible text found in the HTML.
findings.explanation: Fewer than 150 words of text were found in the HTML. Word count is not a ranking factor by itself, and pages rendered with JavaScript may appear thin to this crawler.
findings.suggestion: Check whether the page fully answers its visitors' needs; add useful content if it does not.

findings.title: Low word count
findings.evidence: 3 words of visible text found in the HTML.
findings.explanation: Fewer than 150 words of text were found in the HTML. Word count is not a ranking factor by itself, and pages rendered with JavaScript may appear thin to this crawler.
findings.suggestion: Check whether the page fully answers its visitors' needs; add useful content if it does not.

findings.title: Internal URLs blocked by robots.txt
findings.evidence: 1 internal URL(s) disallowed, e.g. https://shop.example.com/admin/login
findings.explanation: Some internal links point to URLs disallowed by robots.txt. These were not crawled. This is often intentional (e.g. cart or admin pages).
findings.suggestion: Confirm that each blocked path is meant to be hidden from crawlers; unblock any that should be indexed.

limitations: SYNTHETIC DEMO: shop.example.com is a fictional fixture website served from memory. These findings are genuine crawler output for that fixture, not observations of any real company.
Only raw HTML is analysed; JavaScript is never executed, so content rendered client-side may be missed.
robots.txt is always respected; disallowed URLs are not crawled.
Only pages on the same host as the start URL ('www.' treated as equivalent) are crawled.
Severity, priority and health scores are transparent heuristics, not Google metrics or ranking factors.
Length thresholds for titles and descriptions are approximations; search engines truncate by pixel width.
Pages behind logins, paywalls or bot protection are not accessed; such pages may appear as errors.
Results reflect a single point in time; transient server errors can appear and should be re-tested.
